runs.question: What fine does OMB M-25-21 set for an agency that misses its AI strategy deadline?

answer.text:
The OMB M-25-21 excerpts I found do not set a fine for an agency that misses its AI strategy deadline, and I found no penalty language of any kind tied to that deadline.

What the memo does set is the deadline and the consequences it describes. Each CFO Act agency has 180 days from issuance to produce an AI strategy (within 180 days of the memorandum's issuance, CFO Act agencies are to build an AI Strategy aimed at removing barriers to responsible AI use and improving application maturity). The strategies must also be made public (agencies are to use the template OMB provides and post their strategies publicly).

The closest enforcement-like language concerns high-impact AI that underperforms, not the strategy deadline. In that case, agencies must have a plan to stop using the system until they achieve compliance, and must stop using it altogether if risks cannot be mitigated (when high-impact AI is not performing at an appropriate level, agencies must plan to discontinue its use until compliance is achieved, and if proper risk mitigation is not possible, they must cease using it).

The excerpts I retrieved may not cover the whole memo, so I can't rule out a penalty elsewhere. If you need certainty, check the memo's full text or consult OMB.

Passage says agencies must use the AI Strategies template provided by OMB and make their strategies publicly available.
Passage says agencies must plan to discontinue high-impact AI until compliance and cease use if risk mitigation is not possible.
